synthesis:draft.headline: SA1 five‑minute RRP peaked at 4981.0 $/MWh (interval end 2026-07-31 02:05 ACST).
summary: The five‑minute Regional Reference Price (RRP) peak in SA1 was 4981.0 $/MWh at interval end 2026-07-31 02:05 ACST.
Across the investigation window 214 five‑minute intervals met the analysis threshold of 300.0 $/MWh.
Dispatch TOTALDEMAND at the five‑minute price peak (interval end 2026-07-31 02:05 ACST) was 1472.82 MW.

Operational demand for the half‑hour containing the price extreme (half‑hour ending 2026-07-30 17:00 UTC / 2026-07-31 02:30 ACST) was 1466.0 MW and the window maximum operational demand was 2173.0 MW.
Net interchange at the five‑minute peak showed a net flow into SA1 of 82.59 (negative = import).

AEMO market notices in the event window report (a) a non‑credible contingency event in SA on 30/07/2026 [c1], (b) an inter‑regional transfer limit variation notice on 01/08/2026 [c2], and (c) a Forecast Lack Of Reserve Level 1 (LOR1) declaration for SA on 29/07/2026 [c3].

possible_explanations.statement: Low wind generation in SA1 may have reduced available local supply and could have contributed to the high price (need total wind output to check).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Obtain a verified SA1 total wind generation time series (five‑minute or half‑hourly) covering 2026-07-30T04:30:00Z–2026-07-31T05:00:00Z and compare wind output at the event interval to surrounding intervals; cite the total wind MW evidence id.

possible_explanations.statement: Large unit output changes or availability shifts might have reduced supply margin or changed dispatch outcomes.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Review unit‑level dispatch histories, outage and availability notices and the generator offer/bid data around the event interval (with evidence ids) to see whether these SCADA changes correspond to outages, ramping limits or offer changes.

possible_explanations.statement: Interconnector transfer limits or invoked constraint sets (see the Tailem_Bnd notice [c2]) could have limited import/export capability and might have influenced local price formation.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Obtain interconnector transfer limit data, constraint invocation records and detailed constraint equations for the relevant time (with evidence ids) and compare allowed transfer to actual netinterchange at the peak interval.

possible_explanations.statement: Higher-than-expected demand or forecast/actual demand divergence could have contributed to price outcomes.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare predispatch/forecast demand runs to actual operational demand for the 24 half‑hours around the peak (use the forecast_targets_utc) and cite the forecast vs actual MAE or per‑interval forecast errors.

uncertainties: get_generation_change returns SCADA snapshots and largest unit changes but does not label units by technology type in the returned fields, so mapping observed unit changes to 'wind' is uncertain.

get_weather_context returned hourly model-derived WS50M wind speed summaries for a single point (Adelaide) and not a regional, five‑minute wind generation series; it does not provide wind speed at the exact five‑minute price peak with a matching evidence id.
missing_evidence: Total wind generation (MW) time series for SA1 covering 2026-07-30T04:30:00Z–2026-07-31T05:00:00Z at five‑minute or half‑hourly resolution with evidence ids.
A mapping of duids in the generation change output to technology type (which duids are wind farms) or a labelled generator output time series, so SCADA changes can be attributed to wind.
Interconnector transfer limit time series and constraint invocation records covering the event interval with evidence ids (to test whether constraints or limits were binding).
Predispatch/forecast runs and a forecast vs actual comparison (MAE) for the 24 half‑hours around the peak (forecast_targets_utc), with evidence ids.
